title: Breaking Universality in the Lower Order Terms in the 1-level and 2-level Density of Holomorphic Cusp Newforms: the asymptotic formula for $A_{k,N}(\phi)$ (Theorem 3.1)
author: Lawrence Dillon; Xiaoyao Huang; Say-Yeon Kwon; Meiling Laurence; Steven J. Miller; Vishal Muthuvel; Luke Rowen; Pramana Saldin; Steven Zanetti
work: Breaking Universality in the Lower Order Terms in the 1-level and 2-level Density of Holomorphic Cusp Newforms
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the asymptotic evaluation of A_{k,N}(phi) printed as Theorem 3.1 of the paper (native source0.tex lines 471--475), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it (source0.tex lines 476--540, printed as Proof of Theorem 3.1 and closed by the author's own qed at line 540). Section 3 of the paper is the first computation on which both headline level densities rest, and the retained proof is the whole of that section except its one-line introduction. What puts the unit above an ordinary qualifying-examination exercise: (i) the integral of psi(k/4 + 2 pi i x/log R) against phi is not evaluated by a routine Taylor expansion, because the substitution z = 2 pi i x/log R must be justified on a range that itself grows with log R; the author first symmetrises the integrand using that phi is even, subtracts the leading term psi(k/4) phi-hat(0) taken from 8.363.3 of Gradshteyn--Ryzhik, and then needs the symmetric Taylor formula f(z0+z)+f(z0-z)-2f(z0) = f''(z0) z^2 + O(z^4) together with an explicit disc of convergence, which is obtained from Cauchy's inequality on Omega = {z : Re(z) > 0} and gives |x| < k log(R)/(8 pi); (ii) the complementary range |x| >= k log(R)/(8 pi) is not disposed of by compact support, precisely because that range grows with log R, so the author expands psi through its series psi(z) = -gamma + sum over n of (z-1)/((n+1)(n+z)) taken from Abramowitz--Stegun, bounds each term by (8 pi x + |k-4| log R)/n^2, sums in n and finally invokes Schwartz decay of phi to obtain O(1/log^4 R) for the tail; (iii) the same argument is then repeated for the mirrored point z0 = k/4 + 1/2, and the two estimates are combined through the paper's own definition A_{k,N}(phi) = 2 phi-hat(0) log(sqrt(N)/pi) plus the two psi-integrals (retained at lines 302--305) to produce exactly the stated main term -(2 pi^2/log^2 R)(integral of phi(x) x^2 dx)(psi''(k/4) + psi''(k/4+1/2)). Holding the error at O(1/log^4 R) throughout, and realising that the second-order term must be extracted by symmetry instead of brute-force expansion, is a research-paper computation rather than a textbook exercise: the paper needs exactly this 1/log^4 R control because the lower-order terms it studies live at orders log^{-1} and log^{-3}. H2.
